# SME&C Techlabs

> A catalog of templatized Azure use cases as Infrastructure as Code (Bicep and
> Terraform). Every use case is resilient by design, mapped to the Azure
> Well-Architected Framework, ships with dev and prod parameter profiles, and
> carries machine-readable cost metadata that a script prices live against the
> public Azure Retail Prices API.

## How the catalog is organized

- Each use case lives under `catalog/<use-case>/` (landing zones are nested, e.g. `catalog/landing-zone/core`).
- A use case folder contains: `main.bicep` (deployable template), `parameters/dev.bicepparam` and usually `parameters/prod.bicepparam`, `metadata.json` (WAF + cost + what/why), and `README.md`.
- Shared building blocks live under `modules/` and are referenced by templates.
- `metadata.json` is the contract: `what`, `why`, `potentialUseCases`, `category`, `industries`, `compliance`, `wellArchitected` (5 pillars), and `cost.components` (each `fixed` or `usage`).

## Use cases

- [Core Landing Zone](catalog/landing-zone/core/README.md): Log Analytics, hardened Storage, Key Vault, hub VNet + NSG.
- [AI / GenAI Landing Zone](catalog/landing-zone/ai/README.md): Azure AI Services (Foundry), Azure AI Search, Key Vault, Storage, Log Analytics — keyless.
- [Web App](catalog/web-app/README.md): Linux App Service + App Insights + Log Analytics; zone-redundant in prod.
- [Container App](catalog/container-app/README.md): Azure Container Apps with HTTP autoscaling; scale-to-zero in dev.
- [SQL Data API](catalog/sql-data-api/README.md): App Service + Azure SQL, passwordless managed-identity, Entra-only SQL.
- [AI Chat](catalog/ai-chat/README.md): Azure OpenAI gpt-5-mini + App Service + serverless Cosmos DB, keyless.

## Shared modules

- [log-analytics](modules/log-analytics.bicep): Log Analytics workspace.
- [app-insights](modules/app-insights.bicep): workspace-based Application Insights.
- [storage-account](modules/storage-account.bicep): hardened StorageV2 (TLS 1.2, no public blob).
- [key-vault](modules/key-vault.bicep): RBAC-enabled Key Vault with soft delete.
- [private-endpoint](modules/private-endpoint.bicep): generic private endpoint + DNS zone group (industry hardening overlay).

## Cost estimation

- `tools/Get-CatalogCost.ps1 -UseCase <path>` prices one use case; `-All` rolls up the portfolio TCO.
- Prices come live from `https://prices.azure.com/api/retail/prices` (public, no auth). Components are `fixed` (committed monthly) or `usage` (illustrative, from assumed monthly quantities).
- The deploy panel offers advanced options (models/SKUs/sizes/capacities from `site/registry.json`, grouped per service). Changing the region or an option calls `POST /api/estimate`, which reprices the affected components live so the itemized total reflects the chosen SKU, capacity, node/replica count, zone redundancy, and SQL tier.

## Website (gallery)

- `site/` is a static SME&C Techlabs gallery (index.html + assets) that loads `site/catalog.json`.
- `tools/Build-Catalog.ps1` regenerates `site/catalog.json` from every `metadata.json`.
- A FastAPI backend in `site/server/` gates the gallery behind Entra ID, records activity, and provisions/destroys Azure resources with its own managed identity (SQLite system of record on App Service's `/home`). After a successful deploy it grants the signed-in user the Reader role on their own resource group (best-effort, RG-scoped) so they can view the resources in the Azure portal; users signing in from another tenant are first invited as a B2B guest (Microsoft Graph) so the grant has a valid principal. Deployments carry an auto-cleanup end time (default 2 days, max 4) enforced by a background scheduler; failed deploys that left partial resources are cleanable from the account/admin views. See `site/server/README.md`.
- `.github/workflows/deploy-gallery.yml` publishes the gallery to Azure App Service via Azure OIDC on pushes to `main` that touch `site/`, `catalog/`, or `tools/Build-Templates.ps1`.
- Header pages: **Roadmap & retirements** (search by service, collapsible per-service lists of retirements / previews / recent GA from `site/updates.json`) and **Capacity** (collapsible per-service items, each expanding to per-region status, from `site/capacity.json`).

## Live signals

- **Service lifecycle** — `tools/Build-Updates.ps1` maps Azure Updates onto the services each use case provisions and writes `site/updates.json` (refreshed weekly by `.github/workflows/updates.yml`). The use-case modal lists only the upcoming retirements affecting that use case; the full catalog lives on the Roadmap & retirements page.
- **Region capacity** — `tools/Build-Capacity.ps1` probes subscription quota and regional availability across Americas regions for capacity-sensitive services (Azure OpenAI TPM per model/version/SKU, App Service, VM cores + per-family quota, Container Apps, AVS, Fabric, Power BI, Purview) and writes `site/capacity.json` (refreshed daily by `.github/workflows/capacity.yml`). Cards show a "Quota-sensitive" flag; the region picker is colour-coded and model/VM-size aware. Advanced-option dropdowns are backed by `site/registry.json` (`tools/Build-Registry.ps1`, refreshed by `.github/workflows/registry.yml`).

## Submitting a use case

- The gallery's **"+ Submit a use case"** panel accepts a **zip upload** of a ready-to-deploy template (`main.bicep` at the root + at least one `parameters/*.bicepparam`; optional `metadata.json` / `README.md`).
- `POST /api/use-cases/upload` validates the zip (zip-slip guard, size/bomb limits, required files), stages it into the `catalog/<slug>/` layout, then creates a review branch and commits the bundle. Maintainers review via the admin **Submissions** tab and open the PR through a pre-filled compare link (org policy blocks Actions from opening PRs).
- A natural-language path that produces *deployable* templates is tracked in GitHub issue #7 (the earlier AI-drafted-prose flow is parked because its Bicep was not deployable).

## Validation

- `.github/workflows/bicep-validate.yml` builds and lints every `main.bicep`, module, and `.bicepparam` on PR/push.
- Locally: `az bicep build --file <template>` and `az bicep build-params --file <paramfile>`.

## Tailoring for regulated industries

- Landing zones are the same across industries; regulated differences (HLS/HIPAA-HITRUST, FSI, manufacturing, automotive) come from a hardening overlay: private endpoints, customer-managed keys, diagnostic settings, and Azure Policy — opted into via parameters and the `private-endpoint` module, not by forking templates.
- `industries` and `compliance` arrays in each `metadata.json` drive the gallery filters.
